To view your electric rate and other charges and credits specific to your service type, click below for the current rate schedules.
RATE SCHEDULES
Gas Service
Natural gas service is provided to customers in the Reno-Sparks area.
Learn More
In addition to our standard residential and commercial plans, we offer a variety of specialty options that can provide additional savings on your energy bill:
Time-of-Use Option
Customers who are willing to use less electricity during peak demand periods will save money by shifting their usage to times with lower rates. Some could even save 15 percent off their annual electricity bill if they decide to use less electricity during these peak periods.
Learn More
Net Metering
Net metering allows you to use the energy generated by your renewable energy system to offset your monthly power bill. Any customer who installs a renewable energy system may be eligible for net metering.
Learn More
Electric Vehicle Rate Rider
Customers with electric vehicles who are on our special Time-of-Use rates pay a discounted rate if they charge the vehicle during off-peak hours.
Learn More
Expanded Solar Access Program (ESAP)
Our Expanded Solar Access Program (ESAP) allows eligible customers to take advantage of solar energy without having a system on their property.
Learn More
Daily Demand Pricing
Customers who participate in Daily Demand Pricing are incentivized with a lower monthly basic service charge and lower energy consumption rate than customers on the standard rate.
Learn More
Interruptible Irrigation Service
Interruptible Irrigation Service is a subsidized rate for eligible agricultural customers who agree to interruptible irrigation pump service during certain situations. This service is applicable to electricity used solely to pump water to irrigate land for agricultural purposes.
Learn More
NV GreenEnergy Rider
We are committed to working with interested customers to accommodate their renewable energy aspirations. Low-cost renewable energy opportunities are available periodically for eligible customers with larger than one megawatt of demand.
LEARN MORE
Optional Pricing Program Rate
The application for the Optional Pricing Program Rate (NVEOPPR) has been withdrawn from the Public Utilities Commission of Nevada (PUCN). NV Energy plans to resubmit a similar application to the PUCN in the near future.
LEARN MORE

Northern Nevada Gas Rates
Residential Natural Gas Service (Schedule RNG)
Residential Natural Gas service is applicable to all domestic gas serv
[DOC 4] https://www.nvenergy.com/account-services/energy-pricing-plans/gas
ice for space heating, water heating, cooking, air conditioning and other uses. This schedule also applies to churches (chapels other than marriage chapels) and other buildings used for religious worship (provided they are owned and operated by a recognized religious society or corporation other than a religious school).
Liquefied PetroleumGas Service (Schedule LPG)
Liquefied Petroleum Gas service is provided only in the Rainbow Bend area and is currently closed to any new service.
Small Commercial and Industrial Natural Gas Service (Schedule SCNG)
Small Commercial and Industrial Natural Gas service is applicable to commercial and industrial natural gas customers whose monthly gas consumption is less than 12,000 therms during all of the five (5) winter months, November through March.
Large Commercial and Industrial Natural Gas Service (Schedule LCNG)
Large Commercial and Industrial Natural Gas service is applicable to large commercial and industrial natural gas customers whose monthly gas consumption equals or exceeds 12,000 therms during one or more of the five (5) winter months, November through March.

Time-of-Use Rate
Shift Your Usage, Lower Your Bill
You could save money on your bill by changing your habits and using less energy during times of the d
[DOC 5] https://www.nvenergy.com/account-services/energy-pricing-plans/time-of-use
ay when demand is the highest.
Customers who participate in time-of-use (TOU) are rewarded with a lower energy rate during off-peak hours than the standard flat rate.
Residential
How It Works
Energy rates on time-of-use (TOU) vary by the time of day, so the program works best for customers who can shift some of their energy use to off-peak hours, which are times of less demand on the electrical system when the costs to serve customers are lower.
On-peak:
These are times when customers use the most energy. With TOU, energy rates are much higher during on-peak hours, so it's best to shift energy use from this time to the lower-cost hours. It's best to decrease use of washers and dryers, dishwashers, and other high energy-use appliances during these times.
Off-peak:
These are the times when customers use less energy. With TOU, energy rates per kilowatt-hour are lower during off-peak hours than the standard flat rate, so these are the hours when you should use energy most. These are the best times to do laundry, run your pool pump, and use your dishwasher.
See Your Savings
Not sure if TOU is right for you? Get a personalized cost comparison for your account based on your usage history.
Your Cost Comparison
Try It Risk-Free
You can try TOU at no risk for the first year. If after 12 months we find that you did not save money, we will credit the difference and offer to move you back to the standard flat rate.
ENROLL IN TOU
TOU + Electric Vehicle
If you own an electric vehicle and participate in TOU, you receive an even lower rate on all energy use including charging your vehicle during overnight hours.
See Your Savings
Get a personalized look at how much you could save each year by switching to TOU + Electric Vehicle.
Your Cost Comparison
Try It Risk-Free
You can try TOU + Electric Vehicle at no risk for the first year. If after 12 months we find that you did not save money, we will credit the difference and offer to move you back to the standard flat rate.
ENROLL IN TOU + Electric Vehicle
TOU Advanced Rates
You could save even more with our specialized TOU rate, Critical Peak Pricing.
LEARN MORE
Price Comparison
Customers enrolled in TOU participate in variable pricing. Compare the standard flat rate with base TOU rates.
Learn More
More Ways to Save
PowerShift by NV Energy offers a variety of free products and services to help you save energy and money.

Business
How It Works
Energy rates on time-of-use (TOU) vary by the time of day, so the program works best for customers who can shift some of their energy use to off-peak hours, which are times of less demand on the electrical system when the costs to serve customers are lower.
Customers with a large energy demand are required to participate in TOU. Please contact our
Business Solutions Center
if you have questions about TOU related to your business.
On-peak:
These are times when customers use the most energy. With TOU, energy rates are much higher during on-peak ho
[DOC 5] https://www.nvenergy.com/account-services/energy-pricing-plans/time-of-use
urs, so it's best to shift energy use from this time to the lower-cost hours. It's best to decrease use of high energy-use appliances and equipment during these times.
Off-peak:
These are the times when customers use less energy. With TOU, energy rates per kilowatt-hour are lower during off-peak hours than the standard flat rate, so these are the hours when you should use energy most. These are the best times to use high energy-use appliances and equipment.
See Your Savings
Not sure if TOU is right for you? Get a personalized look at how much your business could save each year by switching to TOU.
Your Cost Comparison
ENROLL IN TOU
TOU + Electric Vehicle
If you own an electric vehicle and participate in TOU, you receive an even lower rate on all energy use including charging your vehicle during overnight hours.
See Your Savings
Not sure if TOU is right for you? Get a personalized look at how much your business could save each year by switching to TOU + Electric Vehicle.

PowerShift Business Energy Services
Frequently Asked Questions
Do energy rates vary during the day for customers not on time-of-use?
No. If you do not participate in time-of-use, energy rates are the same no matter the time of day. The lower energy rate available for time-of-use is an incentive for program participants to help conserve energy during peak hours and move energy demand to off-peak hours.
What tools are available to help monitor my energy use?
MyAccount has tools to help you monitor your energy use and manage your account. You can monitor your energy usage by day or down to 15-minute increments to see the times of day your energy use is highest. Making small adjustments could lead to savings on your bill.
What happens if I move?
If you move from one home to another, you will need to opt in to time-of-use for the account at your new address. Your participation in time-of-use does not transfer from one location to another.
Can I cancel my participation in time-of-use?
Enrollment in time-of-use requires participation for a minimum of 12 months. If you must end your enrollment prior to 12 months because you are moving, or for any other reason, you are no longer eligible for the Guaranteed Lowest Rate. Following 12 months on the program, you can cancel your enrollment at any time, and the cancellation will take effect within one to two billing cycles.

Net Metering
Net Metering Rates
Net Metering (NEM) allows you to receive a credit on your bill for excess energy generated by your renewable energy system, 
[DOC 6] https://www.nvenergy.com/account-services/energy-pricing-plans/net-metering
which can help to offset your monthly utility bill energy costs.
Your NV Energy account will be moved to the appropriate net metering rate once your renewable energy system receives permission to operate and begins generating electricity.
The following is information on current net metering rate types.
Northern Nevada
Net Metering Rider-2025 (NMR-2025)
Beginning with applications approved on or after October 1, 2025, NMR-2025 is the default net metering rate for northern Nevada customers with renewable energy systems with a capacity rated less than 25 kilowatts of electricity.
Under the NMR-2025 rate, the difference between the amount of utility-delivered electricity and customer-exported electricity is calculated every 15 minutes. If during a 15-minute period a customer exports more energy to the grid than the customer receives from the utility, each such net excess kilowatt-hour (kWh) is credited monthly at 75% of the current applicable rate.
Net Metering Rider-B (NMR-B)
NMR-B is the default net metering rate for northern Nevada customers with renewable energy systems with a capacity rated more than 25 kilowatts and less than 1,000 kilowatts of electricity.
Under the NMR-B rate, the difference between the amount of utility-generated electricity and customer-generated electricity is calculated every month. Each kilowatt-hour (kWh) of customer-generated electricity that is sent back to the grid is credited monthly at 100% of the current applicable rate.
Questions?
Residential: (775) 834-3020
Commercial: (775) 834-4337
Toll-free: (855) 227-5686
Southern Nevada
Net Metering Rider-405 (NMR-405), Tranche 4
NMR-405 Tranche 4 is the default net metering rate for southern Nevada customers with renewable energy systems with a capacity rated less than 25 kilowatts of electricity.
Under the NMR-405 rate, the difference between the amount of utility-generated electricity and customer-generated electricity is calculated every month. Each kilowatt-hour (kWh) of customer-generated electricity that is sent back to the grid is credited monthly at 75% of the current applicable rate.
Net Metering Rider-B (NMR-B)
NMR-B is the default net metering rate for southern Nevada customers with renewable energy systems with a capacity rated more than 25 kilowatts and less than 1,000 kilowatts of electricity.
Under the NMR-B rate, the difference between the amount of utility-generated electricity and customer-generated electricity is calculated every month. Each kilowatt-hour (kWh) of customer-generated electricity that is sent back to the grid is credited monthly at 100% of the current applicable rate.
Questions?
(702) 402-2330
Toll-free: (844) 882-0767

Electric Vehicle Rate
NV Energy offers special Electric Vehicle Time-of-Use rates that allows customers to pay a discounted rate if they charge the
[DOC 7] https://www.nvenergy.com/account-services/energy-pricing-plans/electric-vehicle
 vehicle during the utility’s electric vehicle charging period (late night to the early morning hours of the day).
Electric Vehicle Time-of-Use rates are higher during daytime and early evening hours (on-peak times when electricity use is highest), lower during nighttime hours (off-peak times when electricity use is lowest). Rates are even lower during late-night and early morning hours (during the electric vehicle charging period).
RATES SCHEDULE
Residential
Benefits of the Electric Vehicle Rate
The discounted rate applies to all of the energy used at a home or apartment during that period of time, not just electricity used to charge an electric vehicle.
To help customers who are uncertain about the best rate for their lifestyle and electric vehicle charging needs, a comparison will be made between the Electric Vehicle Time of Use Rate and the regular flat rate for the first 12-month period. If the Electric Vehicle Time of Use Rate was more costly during that period, NV Energy will credit the difference back to the customer and give the customer the option to move back to the flat rate. There’s no risk in trying the electric vehicle rate program for the first year due to the Guaranteed Lowest Rate* (GLR) feature.
Shifting your on-peak electric usage to off-peak and charging your electric vehicle at night will keep your rates down.
Helps to preserve the environment.
Notice: In order to participate in this electric vehicle rate program, you must allow NV Energy access to your electric meter. Participation, however, is not guaranteed – you must be pre-qualified.
Saving Energy with Electric Vehicle Rate
If your home is generally unoccupied during peak hours, you may experience the greatest benefit from this program.
Use laundry machines, dishwashers, chargers, and other appliances during off-peak hours.
Charge your electric vehicle at night.
During warm months, set your thermostat to 78-80 during peak hours.
Keep unneeded lights off during peak hours.
Consider joining the NV Energy
Smart Thermostat
Program.
If you have or are considering to add solar generation to your home, you may experience added benefit from this program.
You can find more energy saving tips here.
Guaranteed Lowest Rate (GLR)*
If after the first 12-month period, we find that you have spent more on the electric vehicle rate than you would have spent on the standard rate, we will refund the difference and restore you to the standard rate (if you choose). In order to receive the annual savings associated with being on the TOU rate, you are requested to remain on the program for a full 12 months.
How Do I Sign Up?
We encourage you to review your personal energy usage patterns and take the following into account when considering participation in this program:
The Time of Use program has rates that are generally higher in the summer season and lower in the winter season.
Depending on where you live, the weather, and your energy usage patterns, your monthly bills may be higher during t
[DOC 7] https://www.nvenergy.com/account-services/energy-pricing-plans/electric-vehicle
he summer season.
A more optimal time to sign up for the program is during specific times of the year when winter rates are in effect and energy usage is lower.
Signing up when winter rates are in effect will give you time to familiarize yourself with the program when rates and monthly bills are generally lower.
The TOU Rate will become effective on the next full billing cycle after the TOU meter is installed and stay in effect for twelve months.
NV Energy requires full physical access monthly to this TOU meter.
All NV Energy rates are subject to change by the Nevada Public Utility Commission.
NV Energy is authorized to release billing and load information to agents of NV Energy Company for the sole purpose of providing services relating to the TOU Rate program.
NV Energy guarantees that customers participating in the TOU Rate will not spend more for electricity in the first year billed on the TOU Rate than they would have been billed on the Standard Rate.
Sign Up Online
< back to Electric Vehicles
Business
Things to Consider:
We encourage you to review the energy usage patterns for your business and take the following into account when considering participation in this program:
The optional Time of Use program has rates that are generally higher in the summer season and lower in the winter season which makes the winter season an optimal time to sign-up for the program.
Signing up when winter rates are in effect will give you time to familiarize yourself with the program when rates and monthly bills are generally lower.
Depending on where your business is located, the weather, and your energy usage patterns, your monthly bills may be higher during the summer season.
The optional TOU Rate will become effective on the next full billing cycle after the TOU meter is installed and stay in effect for a minimum term of one year and will continue on a month to month basis thereafter.
NV Energy requires full physical access monthly to the TOU meter.
All NV Energy rates are subject to change by the Nevada Public Utilities Commission.
NV Energy is authorized to release billing and load information to agents of NV Energy for the sole purpose of providing services relating to the TOU Rate program.
How Do I Sign Up?
Sign Up Online
